To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) protein translocation channels are highly dynamic structures that are regulated by a multitude of regulatory factors; (ii) the channel properties of protein translocation pores depend on the composition of the channel complex and the presence of the regulatory factors; and (iii) the protein transport pores are able to discriminate between different preproteins and thus are able to select the right protein for the correct destination.

the protein import machinaries of mitochondria, chloroplasts, and the ER have a common ancestor, that the translocation pores are composed of multiple subunits and that these pores are highly dynamic structures.
the protein translocation systems of the chloroplast and the mitochondrial outer membrane are highly selective, gated, voltage-dependent channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of protein translocators of the chloroplast and mitochondrial protein import systems, and the identification and characterization of the pore forming subunit of the endoplasmatic reticulum translocating complex Sec61.
the identification of the channel moities of protein translocases, the determination of their molecular properties and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying their regulation.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms and regulation of the protein translocation systems in chloroplasts and the endoplasmatic reticulum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular properties of the individual subunits which form the protein translocation pores are still not fully elucidated.
the planar bilayers are an excellent model system to investigate protein translocation channels and their regulation.
the planar lipid membrane technique has been a valuable tool for the characterization of protein translocases and for the exploration of the mechanisms of their regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility of the planar lipid membrane technique for the characterization of protein translocases and the regulation of these protein import pores.

single channel electrophysiologial techniques have provided a powerful tool for the identification and characterization of the individual components of protein import channels of the chloroplast and mitochondrial inner membrane and the endoplasmatic reticulum.

single channel electrophysics has provided a powerful method to study the protein translocation pores of the three main protein translocation systems in eukaryotes, the chloroplast, the mitochondrion and the endoplasmatic reticulum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein translocation channels of the various subcellular organelles have very similar properties.
the planar bilayers have been instrumental in the identification and characterization of protein translocases and their subunits.
planar bilayer electrophysiology is a powerful tool to study the molecular mechanisms of protein translocation and to characterize the individual channel subunits forming the protein import pore.
